description_en: Jagamaru Pukhū Phalcā (N: 'aphalcāin a pond without a foundation') stands in the centre of the Pimbahāḥ Pukhū (pond), also known as Jagamadu Pukhū (N: 'the water tank without a foundation'). Thephalcāis reached by walking through the Jagamaru Pukhū Phalcā (LAL4218) on the western side of the pond and then crossing over a narrow bridge. The shape of thephalcāchanged several times over the past decades. The tile roof used to rest on wooden pillars and was open on all sides, later, it was walled in, received doors and windows and was covered with a tin roof. For a while it was used as a library (Pruscha1975: C/P-75). In circa 1998, GTZ/udle supported thephalcā's reconstruction to its original configuration: supported by 12 newly carved pillars, open to all sides and covered with a traditonal tile (jhĩgaṭī) roof. The pillars were carved in a hybrid design with modern carvings on the shafts and traditional motifs on the upper registers. Thephalcācollapsed in the earthquakes in 2015 and was reconstructed in 2017.A small shrine dedicated to LordKṛṣṇais located  to the east of thephalcā.
description_ne: यो जगमरु पुखू फल्चा पिंबाहाल पोखरीको बीचमा रहेको छ जुन पोखरीलाई जगमदु पुखु (जगविनाको पोखरी) पनि भनिन्छ । फल्चाको छानो झिँगटीले छाइएको छ । पोखरीको दक्षिणतर्फ रहेको अर्को पिम्बाहा फल्चा (LAL4218) हुँदै यस फल्चामा जाने साँघुरो पुल रहेको छ । पहिला यो फल्चा चारैतर्फ खुला रहेको, काष्ठस्तम्भद्वारा उठाइएको र छाना टायलले छाइएको थियो । तर पछि यसको चारैतर्फ गाह्रो लगाइयो र जस्ताको छाना हालियो, फल्चा झ्यालढोका समेत भएको एउटा कोठाको रूपमा परिणत भयो (Pruscha1975: C/P-75) । त्यसपछि सन् १९९८ तिर GTZ/udle ले १२ वटा काष्ठस्तम्भ राखी पुरानो स्वरूपमा फल्चाको पुनर्निर्माण गर्न सुरु गर्यो । धेरैले फल्चा बनेपछि आफ्नो पुरानै स्वरूपमा फर्किएको बताउने गर्दथे । फल्चाभित्र कुनै देवताको मूर्ति छैन तर पूर्वपट्टि श्रीकृष्णको सानो मन्दिर रहेको छ ।सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पमा यो फल्चा ध्वस्त भएको थियो । अहिले फेरि मौलिक स्वरूपमा नै यसको पुनर्निर्माण भएको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The Lalitpur Sub-metropolitan office renovated the pond and the gatewayphalcā(LAL4218) at the cost of 50.000.00 Lakh Nepali rupees.
Following its collapse in the 2015 earthquakes, thephalcāwas reconstructed in 2016. The Lalitpur Metropolitan Office contributed 800.000 rupees and local private donors 160.000 rupees.

Jagamaru Pukhū Phalcā is said to have been built by Lākhes from Pimbahal, though the concrete date is unknown. According toU. Śreṣṭha(2012), thebhajana phalcāand the small Kṛṣṇa temple were destroyed during the earthquake of 1934and later rebuilt by Subbā (government officer) Motilal Shrestha (Lākhe). It is said that Subbā brought a tree over the river Bagmati to Pimbahal with the permission of the then Rana Prime minister Juddha Shamsher and consequently rebuilt the temple andphalcāin 1940 CE.

Subbā Motilāla Śreṣṭha (from the Lākhe clan) of Pimbahal reconstructed Jagamaru Pukhū Phalcā and the small Krishna temple in the 1940s.According to Ratneswor Lal Shrestha, 76, his grandfather Motilal Shrestha rebuilt thephalcāin the 1940s CE. The donors of thephalcāare unknown. Jagamaru Pukhū Phalcā's was converted into a one-story building with door and windows and covered with a tin roof. A library was run inside.

In circa 1998, GTZ/udle supported thephalcā's reconstruction to its original configuration: supported by 12 newly carved pillars, open to all sides and covered with a traditonal tile (jhĩgaṭī) roof. The pillars were carved in a hybrid design with modern carvings on the shafts and traditional motifs on the upper registers.
